channel.title: The Chest Mount blog
channel.description: Police bodycam incident breakdowns and explainers.

item.title: Beaverton Police Chase Bodycam: Is Attempting to Elude a Felony in Oregon?
item.description: Beaverton, OR police released bodycam of a late-night chase that ended in a crash, a foot search with a K-9 and a DUII arrest. How Oregon's eluding law (ORS 811.540) treats running in a car vs. on foot, plus reckless driving and DUII. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Lee County Zombie Traffic Stop: Warning vs. Ticket for Speeding in Florida
item.description: A Lee County, FL deputy stopped a driver dressed as a zombie for going 48 in a 30 on Halloween night and let him go with a warning. How officer discretion works at traffic stops, what Florida's speed laws (316.183, 316.189) say, and the fines and points a speeding ticket can carry. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Ohio Troopers Nearly Hit During a Sobriety Test: Drug-Impaired OVI, Field Sobriety Tests and the Move Over Law
item.description: Ohio State Highway Patrol video shows an SUV narrowly missing two Toledo Post troopers and a woman during a field sobriety test, then hitting the patrol car. What reports say, how drug-impaired OVI works under ORC 4511.19 and what Ohio's move over law requires. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Timberlake Police Cruiser Hit During Traffic Stop: What OVI and Ohio's Move Over Law Mean
item.description: A Timberlake, OH officer had stepped out of his cruiser about 20 seconds before a suspected impaired driver hit it. What police and news reports say, what OVI means under ORC 4511.19 and what Ohio's move over law (ORC 4511.213) requires. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Holbrook Police Burning Jeep Rescue: What OUI Second Offense Means in Massachusetts
item.description: Holbrook, MA officers pulled a trapped driver from a burning Jeep, and police are seeking an OUI second offense summons. What happened, what M.G.L. c. 90 §24 says about a second OUI, and how a summons works. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Lee County PIT Maneuver Bodycam: What Is a PIT Maneuver, and Is It Legal?
item.description: Lee County, FL deputies used a PIT maneuver to end a North Fort Myers chase, and the bodycam caught the driver asking for a cigarette. What a PIT maneuver is, when it's legal, and what Florida's fleeing (316.1935) and reckless driving (316.192) laws say. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: Winter Springs Police Tesla Video: Fleeing vs. Not Seeing the Lights
item.description: A Tesla's cameras became key evidence after a Winter Springs, FL driver was accused of fleeing police. What Florida's fleeing and eluding law (316.1935) says, why video matters and what to do if you're unsure. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: When Refusing to Leave Goes Wrong: Marion, IL Bodycam Breakdown
item.description: A neutral, minute-by-minute breakdown of the Marion, Illinois police bodycam footage from March 26, 2026: a trespass warning, a refusal to leave, taser use and what officers say afterward.

item.title: Buffalo Grove Bodycam: "Am I Being Detained?" A Parking-Lot Encounter Breakdown
item.description: A neutral breakdown of Buffalo Grove, Illinois police bodycam footage from August 10, 2024: questions about leaving, a phone, identification, detention vs. arrest and an obstruction arrest.

item.title: Peoria Traffic Stop Bodycam: The "Show vs. Hand Over" License Argument
item.description: A neutral breakdown of Peoria, Illinois police bodycam footage from January 16, 2025: a dragging drill, a dispute over showing vs. handing over a driver's license, an order to exit and a taser deployment.

item.title: Detained vs. Arrested: What's the Difference? (Know Your Rights Basics)
item.description: A plain-English guide to consensual encounters, investigative detentions (Terry stops) and arrests, plus identification, phones and why bodycam encounters escalate. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: How Police Bodycam Footage Becomes Public: FOIA and Public-Records Requests Explained
item.description: How real police bodycam footage gets released: federal FOIA vs. state public-records laws, how to request footage, common exemptions, redactions, fees and appeals. General information, not legal advice.

item.title: How to Watch Police Bodycam Footage Critically: 9 Things to Keep in Mind
item.description: Bodycam video feels like the full truth, but it isn't. Nine practical ways to watch police bodycam footage critically: camera angle, missing context, audio, editing, charges vs. convictions and more.

item.title: What Does "Drive-Stun" Mean? Taser Modes Explained for Bodycam Viewers
item.description: What officers mean by "drive-stun" vs. firing a taser's probes, why the difference matters, and what you can and can't tell from taser bodycam footage. General, non-technical overview.

item.title: What Is a Trespass Warning? How It Generally Works
item.description: What a trespass warning (trespass notice) is, who can issue one, how police are involved, what happens if you return, and why public property is complicated. Laws vary by state; not legal advice.

item.title: Why Police Bodycam Footage Matters for Transparency
item.description: Why public access to real police bodycam footage matters: accountability, public trust, education, better training and an accurate record, plus the privacy limits that should come with it.
